analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. I found no production code, auth, crypto, attestation or wire-contract changes in the supplied units.

Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 389-391) adds a .toolCallDelta case to the collect() switch, which keeps completed calls. This is needed so the test compiles against a new streaming event, and it changes no runtime security behavior. The live canary is gated by the DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_QWEN36 env vars. Its hardcoded default paths point at a developer temp directory and are only read when the gate is on. The canary sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, so it does not exercise the T-041 SSD cache tier.

ReasoningPromptProbeTests.swift (head lines 53-82) adds tests for a new ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix signature with modelType and seedsPlainTailContent parameters. A plain Qwen3-VL tail starts in content, while close-only Qwen models and other model types keep nil. This is parser-state logic, not a confidentiality control. The production change is not in this batch, so its correctness is unverified. A wrong seed could misroute reasoning versus content output channels, which is a functional concern and not a visible security regression.

StreamedToolCallTests.swift is a new test file whose patch excerpt is truncated, so only its first lines were seen. It tests streaming tool-call fragments (streamToolCallDeltas, NativeToolStreamRouter). The production streaming of tool-call deltas is outside this batch. The integration pass should confirm that tool-call deltas are encrypted per hop like other chunks (T-008, fail-closed encryption) and that tool arguments cannot leak plaintext on encryption failure.

No findings from the supplied evidence. Production changes for plain-tail seeding and tool-call delta streaming were not supplied, so coverage of those is limited.
